title: Games Night Charity Iftar - Cyber Security & Computer Science Collaboration
description: A joint charity iftar and games night run by the BCU Cyber Security Society and BCU Computer Science Society. All 45 tickets sold out in 72 hours. Members played Valorant, CS2, Uno, Chess, table tennis, and console games, then shared a three-course iftar meal. It was a relaxed cross-course social where people met new students, caught up with friends, and enjoyed some friendly competition.

title: Debate Night - Cyber Security & Law Collaboration
description: A joint debate night with the BCU Law, Debating and Mooting Society. We started with short individual two-minute arguments, then moved into team debates with mixed groups from both societies. Teams were judged on argument quality, evidence, clarity, and rebuttal strength. It was a great way to test cyber and legal viewpoints on real policy questions. Food and drinks were provided.

title: Cyber Security Mini-Hackathon (Cyberthon Mini 2026)
description: A 3-hour mini-hackathon with one intentionally playful brief: build the most creatively annoying security app you can. Teams quickly prototyped ideas that interrupt risky behaviour and push users toward safer habits. The emphasis was on clear reasoning and working proof-of-concepts, not polish. Each team pitched at the end, and the winning team received a £50 prize. Iftar, snacks, and drinks were provided.

title: Cyber Security Hackathon (Cyberthon 2026)
description: A 5-hour technical hackathon where 50+ students built security prototypes under time pressure. Teams chose one of three challenges: threat detection from raw logs, privilege escalation and IAM risk analysis, or AI app security against prompt injection. By the end, each team delivered a working prototype and a short pitch to judges. Snacks and drinks were available throughout.

title: Semester-Long TryHackMe CTF Series
description: A 12-week TryHackMe series with three labs released each week. Topics included OSINT, forensics, reverse engineering, malware, cryptography, networking, pen testing, and web security. Members could work through the rooms all semester with support available.

title: Game Off 2025 Collaboration
description: Weekly Wednesday sessions with Cyber Security, Computer Science, and Data Science societies to plan and build entries for Itch.io Game Off 2025. Sessions covered brainstorming, prototyping, gameplay work, reverse engineering, and shared security review.

title: Bi-Weekly Online Meets
description: Online meetups every other week for games, open discussion, event planning, and idea sharing. A simple way for members to stay connected between in-person sessions.

title: BCU Open Day (Computing Stand)
description: Represented the Cyber Security Society at the BCU Open Day. Spoke with prospective computing and cybersecurity students, introduced the society's purpose and activities, and supported course leaders during demonstrations.

title: Cyber Security Awareness Event
description: Talks on the impact of cybercrime, cybersecurity career paths, phishing challenges, Google phishing game, sender-verification exercises, Kahoot quiz, and pizza.

title: Big Welcome 2025 Stall
location: BCU Big Welcome Fair, City Centre Campus
description: The society's launch event at the Big Welcome Fair. Helped new students across tech degrees, answered questions, gave demos, and led to a 760% membership increase (from 5 to 40+ members).
